questions.subject: Anatomy
questions.question: Which of the following represents the surface marking of the aortic valve?

options.text: Sternal end of left third costal cartilage
Sternal end of the right third costal cartilage
Beside the sternum in the left third intercostal space
Beside the sternum in right third intercostal space

questions.correctAnswerText: Beside the sternum in the left third intercostal space
questions.explanation: The surface marking of the aortic valve is beside the sternum in the left third intercostal space. The source figure shows the relation of the cardiac valves to the thoracic cage.
questions.structuredExplanationText: The surface marking of the aortic valve is beside the sternum in the left third intercostal space. The source figure shows the relation of the cardiac valves to the thoracic cage.

questions.subject: Anatomy
questions.question: What is the surface marking of the mitral valve?

options.text: Behind the sternum end of the left 4th costal cartilage
Behind the sternal end of the right 4th costal cartilage
Left 4th intercostal space in midclavicular line
Left 3rd intercostal space in midclavicular line

questions.correctAnswerText: Behind the sternum end of the left 4th costal cartilage
questions.explanation: The mitral valve orifice is level with the left half of the sternum opposite the left fourth costal cartilage. The source represents it by a line approximately 3 cm long descending to the right.
questions.structuredExplanationText: The mitral valve orifice is level with the left half of the sternum opposite the left fourth costal cartilage. The source represents it by a line approximately 3 cm long descending to the right.

questions.subject: Anatomy
questions.question: A patient developed hoarseness due to left recurrent laryngeal nerve weakness. TTE revealed compression of the nerve by the enlarged base of the heart. Which of the following chambers is likely to be dilated?
questions.explanation: The base of the heart is formed mainly by the left atrium, so left atrial enlargement can compress the left recurrent laryngeal nerve and cause hoarseness. The base is quadrilateral, directed posteriorly, and consists mainly of the left atrium with a small part of the right atrium and the proximal portions of the superior vena cava, inferior vena cava and pulmonary veins. In the supine position it lies approximately opposite T5-T8. The apex is formed by the left ventricle in the fifth intercostal space. The sternocostal surface is formed by right atrium, right ventricle and left ventricle; the diaphragmatic and left surfaces are mainly left ventricle, and the right surface is mainly right atrium.

questions.subject: Anatomy
questions.question: The region marked corresponds to the surface marking for which of the following structures:
questions.explanation: The marked region corresponds to the surface marking of the right atrium. The source describes the right cardiac border as a laterally convex line from the third to the sixth right costal cartilage approximately 1-2 cm lateral to the sternal edge. It also reviews the other borders: upper border from the second left costal cartilage to the third right costal cartilage, inferior border from the sixth right costal cartilage to the apex, and left border from the apex superomedially to the second left costal cartilage.

questions.subject: Anatomy
questions.question: A 30-year-old man was brought to the emergency department after a car accident. He sustained a severe injury to the anterior chest wall from the impact caused by the steering wheel. X-ray revealed fracture of the body of the sternum. Which of the following chambers of the heart is most likely to be injured?
questions.explanation: The right ventricle is most likely to be injured because it forms the major part of the sternocostal surface and lies directly posterior to the sternum, separated from the anterior thoracic wall mainly by the pericardium.
questions.structuredExplanationText: The right ventricle is most likely to be injured because it forms the major part of the sternocostal surface and lies directly posterior to the sternum, separated from the anterior thoracic wall mainly by the pericardium.

questions.subject: Anatomy
questions.question: During the post-mortem heart examination of a patient, the resident palpates a muscular ridge, which is the site of origin of pectinate muscles. In which of the following chambers is the resident palpating this structure?
questions.explanation: The ridge is the crista terminalis in the right atrium. It extends along the atrial wall from the opening of the superior vena cava toward the inferior vena cava, corresponds externally to the sulcus terminalis, and gives origin to the pectinate muscles. It separates the smooth posterior part of the right atrium from the rough anterior part; the venae cavae open into the smooth posterior region.

questions.subject: Anatomy
questions.question: The right border of the heart is formed by which of the following structures?
questions.explanation: The right border of the heart is formed by the right atrium. The source summarizes the cardiac borders as: right - right atrium; left - mostly left ventricle with a small contribution from the left atrial appendage; inferior - mostly right ventricle with a small contribution from left ventricle; upper - left atrium together with the ascending aorta and pulmonary trunk.

questions.subject: Anatomy
questions.question: While doing the doppler USG of a fetal heart, you note blood flow from the right atrium to the left atrium. After the delivery, the connection eventually closes. What would form the floor of this structure after it closes?
questions.explanation: The fetal interatrial communication is the foramen ovale. After closure it forms the fossa ovalis. The floor of the fossa ovalis is the remnant of the septum primum, while its limbus is derived from the septum secundum.
questions.structuredExplanationText: The fetal interatrial communication is the foramen ovale. After closure it forms the fossa ovalis. The floor of the fossa ovalis is the remnant of the septum primum, while its limbus is derived from the septum secundum.

questions.subject: Anatomy
questions.question: What is the location of the sinoatrial node?
questions.explanation: The source explanation describes the sinoatrial node as lying in the upper part of the crista terminalis at the junction of the superior vena cava opening and the right atrium, at the junction between the parts of the right atrium derived from the sinus venosus and primitive atrium. The question, however, presents answer combinations using numbers 1-5 without showing the numbered definitions on the rendered question page. The printed answer key marks option D.

questions.subject: Anatomy
questions.question: A cardiologist is doing the AV node ablation procedure for AVNRT. While locating the AV node, he would look at all of the following landmarks forming its boundary except:
questions.explanation: The posterior leaflet of the tricuspid valve is not a boundary of the triangle of Koch. The atrioventricular node lies centrally within the triangle of Koch on the smooth posterior part of the right atrium. The source gives its boundaries as the coronary sinus, tendon of Todaro and the septal cusp/leaflet of the tricuspid valve.
questions.structuredExplanationText: The posterior leaflet of the tricuspid valve is not a boundary of the triangle of Koch. The atrioventricular node lies centrally within the triangle of Koch on the smooth posterior part of the right atrium. The source gives its boundaries as the coronary sinus, tendon of Todaro and the septal cusp/leaflet of the tricuspid valve.

questions.subject: Anatomy
questions.question: Which of the following statements is false regarding the SA node?

options.text: It is located at the right border of ascending aorta
It contains specialized nodal cardiac muscle
It is supplied by the atrial branches of the right coronary artery
Action potential generated here does not have phase 1 or 2

questions.correctAnswerText: It is located at the right border of ascending aorta
questions.explanation: The false statement is that the sinoatrial node is located at the right border of the ascending aorta. The source places the SA node at the opening of the superior vena cava into the right atrium. It contains specialized nodal cardiac muscle and acts as the pacemaker, is supplied by atrial branches of the right coronary artery, and its action potential lacks phases 1 and 2.
questions.structuredExplanationText: The false statement is that the sinoatrial node is located at the right border of the ascending aorta. The source places the SA node at the opening of the superior vena cava into the right atrium. It contains specialized nodal cardiac muscle and acts as the pacemaker, is supplied by atrial branches of the right coronary artery, and its action potential lacks phases 1 and 2.

questions.subject: Anatomy
questions.question: A 40-year-old man underwent coronary artery bypass grafting. During the procedure, the surgeon applied a clamp to the vessel lying anterior to the transverse pericardial sinus. Identify the vessel.
questions.explanation: The aorta lies anterior to the transverse pericardial sinus. The source explains that serous pericardial reflections form one tube around the aorta and pulmonary trunk and another around the venae cavae and pulmonary veins. The oblique sinus is a J-shaped recess posterior to the left atrium, while the transverse sinus is the passage between these arterial and venous reflections. The aorta and pulmonary trunk lie anterior to the transverse sinus, with the superior vena cava and atria posterior. This permits clamping of the great arterial outflow vessels during cardiac surgery.

questions.subject: Anatomy
questions.question: How many papillary muscles are there in the left ventricle?
questions.explanation: The left ventricle contains two papillary muscles: anterior and posterior. The source contrasts this with the right ventricle, which has three papillary muscles: anterior, posterior and septal.
questions.structuredExplanationText: The left ventricle contains two papillary muscles: anterior and posterior. The source contrasts this with the right ventricle, which has three papillary muscles: anterior, posterior and septal.

questions.subject: Anatomy
questions.question: What are Purkinje fibers?
questions.explanation: Purkinje fibers are modified cardiac muscle fibers. They form a subendocardial conducting network; excitation proceeds from the endocardial surface toward the epicardium.
questions.structuredExplanationText: Purkinje fibers are modified cardiac muscle fibers. They form a subendocardial conducting network; excitation proceeds from the endocardial surface toward the epicardium.

questions.subject: Anatomy
questions.question: A surgeon opens the pericardial sac anteriorly during surgery. He passes a surgical clamp through the transverse sinus. The circulation of blood in which of the following structures is stopped/diverted by his action?
questions.explanation: Passing a clamp through the transverse pericardial sinus allows occlusion/diversion of the aorta and pulmonary trunk. The transverse sinus separates the arterial end of the heart from the venous end: the aorta and pulmonary trunk lie anterior to the sinus and the superior vena cava lies posteriorly.

questions.subject: Anatomy
questions.question: A cardiologist while reviewing a case of MI, notes that the patient has right dominant circulation. Which of the following determines coronary dominance?
questions.explanation: Coronary dominance is determined by the artery that gives rise to the posterior interventricular artery. The source states that in about 65% the posterior interventricular artery arises from the right coronary artery (right dominance), in about 10% from the left coronary/circumflex system (left dominance), and in the remaining cases both systems contribute (balanced dominance).
questions.structuredExplanationText: Coronary dominance is determined by the artery that gives rise to the posterior interventricular artery. The source states that in about 65% the posterior interventricular artery arises from the right coronary artery (right dominance), in about 10% from the left coronary/circumflex system (left dominance), and in the remaining cases both systems contribute (balanced dominance).

questions.subject: Anatomy
questions.question: Coronary angiography of a patient revealed posterior interventricular artery branching from the circumflex artery. What would the arterial circulation in this patient be called?
questions.explanation: If the posterior interventricular artery arises from the circumflex branch of the left coronary artery, the circulation is left dominant. The source again notes the approximate patterns: about 65% right dominance and about 10% left dominance.
questions.structuredExplanationText: If the posterior interventricular artery arises from the circumflex branch of the left coronary artery, the circulation is left dominant. The source again notes the approximate patterns: about 65% right dominance and about 10% left dominance.

questions.subject: Anatomy
questions.question: All of the following are true about the right coronary artery except _____

options.text: It's diameter is less than left coronary artery
It arises from the anterior aortic sinus
It gives rise to circumflex coronary branch
Right conal artery is it's first branch

questions.correctAnswerText: It gives rise to circumflex coronary branch
questions.explanation: The right coronary artery does not give rise to the circumflex coronary artery. It arises from the anterior aortic sinus (right coronary sinus) of the ascending aorta, passes anteriorly and then descends in the coronary sulcus between the right atrium and right ventricle, and turns posteriorly at the inferior margin onto the diaphragmatic surface/base. Its diameter is less than that of the left coronary artery and the right conal artery is usually its first branch. The source explicitly states that the circumflex coronary artery is a branch of the left coronary artery and is the 'exclusive supplier to the right bundle branch'; this source wording is preserved as printed.

It arises from the anterior aortic sinus (right coronary sinus) of the ascending aorta, passes anteriorly and then descends in the coronary sulcus between the right atrium and right ventricle, and turns posteriorly at the inferior margin onto the diaphragmatic surface/base. Its diameter is less than that of the left coronary artery and the right conal artery is usually its first branch. The source explicitly states that the circumflex coronary artery is a branch of the left coronary artery and is the 'exclusive supplier to the right bundle branch'; this source wording is preserved as printed.

questions.subject: Anatomy
questions.question: A 55-year-old man presented with angina. Coronary angiography revealed a block in the right coronary artery. Blood supply through which of the following arteries would not be affected?
questions.explanation: The circumflex artery is a branch of the left coronary artery and therefore is not directly affected by a right-coronary-artery blockage. The source lists branches of the right coronary artery as the right conal artery, artery to the SA node, acute right marginal artery, posterior interventricular artery in the majority, and atrial/anterior/posterior ventricular branches.
questions.structuredExplanationText: The circumflex artery is a branch of the left coronary artery and therefore is not directly affected by a right-coronary-artery blockage. questions.subject: Anatomy
questions.question: All of the following supply the marked structure except:
questions.explanation: The marked structure is the right ventricle. The diagonal artery does not supply it; the diagonal artery is a branch of the anterior interventricular artery and supplies the left ventricle. The right ventricle is supplied predominantly by the right coronary artery and its marginal branch, while the anterior interventricular artery gives one or two anterior right-ventricular branches.

questions.subject: Anatomy
questions.question: A patient underwent angioplasty with a Sirolimus-eluting stent in the anterior interventricular artery. This artery is a branch of:
questions.explanation: The anterior interventricular artery (left anterior descending artery) is a terminal branch of the left coronary artery. The left coronary artery arises from the left aortic sinus/left posterior sinus, passes between the pulmonary trunk and left auricle in the coronary sulcus, and divides into the anterior interventricular artery and circumflex artery. The circumflex gives the left marginal/obtuse marginal branch supplying the left ventricle.
questions.structuredExplanationText: The anterior interventricular artery (left anterior descending artery) is a terminal branch of the left coronary artery. The left coronary artery arises from the left aortic sinus/left posterior sinus, passes between the pulmonary trunk and left auricle in the coronary sulcus, and divides into the anterior interventricular artery and circumflex artery. The circumflex gives the left marginal/obtuse marginal branch supplying the left ventricle.

questions.subject: Anatomy
questions.question: In a patient with STEMI, nuclear stress test revealed poor blood supply to the anterior two-thirds of the interventricular septum. Which of the following blood vessels is most likely to be blocked?
questions.explanation: The anterior two-thirds of the interventricular septum is supplied by the left coronary artery through its anterior interventricular branch. The source contrasts right-coronary distribution (right atrium, most right ventricle, variable diaphragmatic left ventricle, posteroinferior one-third of the interventricular septum, part of left atrium and conduction tissue) with left-coronary distribution (left atrium, left ventricle, a narrow strip of right ventricle and the anterior two-thirds of the interventricular septum).

options.text: Artery from the left posterior aortic sinus

questions.explanation: The blue dotted outline marks the triangle of Koch. In the majority of individuals its arterial supply is derived from the right coronary artery.

questions.subject: Anatomy
questions.question: A patient with a recent MI underwent coronary angiography, which revealed a block in the anterior interventricular artery. The infarction is likely to be present in which of the following regions of the heart?

options.text: Anterior wall of the left ventricle
Inferior surface of the right ventricle

questions.correctAnswerText: Anterior wall of the left ventricle
questions.explanation: Occlusion of the left anterior descending/anterior interventricular artery causes infarction of the anterior wall of the left ventricle. The artery supplies the anterior two-thirds of the interventricular septum and adjacent anterior left-ventricular wall. The source notes that the posterior interventricular artery supplies the posterior septum and inferior right ventricle, while the circumflex artery supplies the left lateral surface.
questions.structuredExplanationText: Occlusion of the left anterior descending/anterior interventricular artery causes infarction of the anterior wall of the left ventricle. The artery supplies the anterior two-thirds of the interventricular septum and adjacent anterior left-ventricular wall. The source notes that the posterior interventricular artery supplies the posterior septum and inferior right ventricle, while the circumflex artery supplies the left lateral surface.

questions.subject: Anatomy
questions.question: Which of the following is not a tributary of the coronary sinus?
questions.explanation: The anterior cardiac vein is not a tributary of the coronary sinus; it drains directly into the right atrium. The source lists tributaries of the coronary sinus as the great cardiac vein, middle cardiac vein, small cardiac vein, posterior cardiac vein and oblique vein of the left atrium. Thebesian veins/venae cordis minimae, anterior cardiac veins and the right marginal vein drain directly into the right atrium.

questions.subject: Anatomy
questions.question: Where does the great cardiac vein lie?

options.text: Anterior part of the coronary sulcus
Posterior part of the right coronary sulcus

questions.explanation: The great cardiac vein lies in the anterior interventricular sulcus. It begins at the cardiac apex, ascends in the anterior interventricular groove to the atrioventricular groove, then passes leftward and posteriorly to enter the coronary sinus at its origin. It accompanies the anterior interventricular artery (left anterior descending artery).
questions.structuredExplanationText: The great cardiac vein lies in the anterior interventricular sulcus. It begins at the cardiac apex, ascends in the anterior interventricular groove to the atrioventricular groove, then passes leftward and posteriorly to enter the coronary sinus at its origin. questions.subject: Anatomy
questions.question: Which of the following statements is true regarding the coronary sinus?

options.text: It lies in the anterior part of coronary sulcus
It ends in the right atrium
It has venae cordis minimae as its tributaries
It develops from the right anterior cardinal vein

questions.correctAnswerText: It ends in the right atrium
questions.explanation: The coronary sinus ends in the right atrium. It develops from the left horn of the sinus venosus and lies in the posterior part of the atrioventricular groove. It opens into the right atrium between the opening of the inferior vena cava and the right atrioventricular orifice. Venae cordis minimae drain directly into the nearest heart chamber and can open into all four chambers.
questions.structuredExplanationText: The coronary sinus ends in the right atrium. It develops from the left horn of the sinus venosus and lies in the posterior part of the atrioventricular groove. It opens into the right atrium between the opening of the inferior vena cava and the right atrioventricular orifice. Venae cordis minimae drain directly into the nearest heart chamber and can open into all four chambers.

questions.subject: Anatomy
questions.question: A 58-year-old man is undergoing coronary artery bypass grafting. The coronary angiography revealed total blockage of the posterior descending artery. While exposing this artery during the procedure, which accompanying vessel is most likely to be injured?
questions.explanation: The middle cardiac vein lies in the posterior interventricular groove accompanying the posterior descending/posterior interventricular artery and is therefore most likely to be injured while exposing that artery.
questions.structuredExplanationText: The middle cardiac vein lies in the posterior interventricular groove accompanying the posterior descending/posterior interventricular artery and is therefore most likely to be injured while exposing that artery.

questions.subject: Anatomy
questions.question: Which among the following is wrong about the venous drainage of the heart?

options.text: Coronary sinus is guarded by the Thebesian valve
Middle cardiac vein lies in the posterior atrioventricular groove
Great cardiac vein accompanies left anterior descending artery
Venae cordis minimae open into all 4 chambers

questions.correctAnswerText: Middle cardiac vein lies in the posterior atrioventricular groove
questions.explanation: The wrong statement is that the middle cardiac vein lies in the posterior atrioventricular groove; the source places it in the posterior interventricular groove. The opening of the coronary sinus may be guarded by the semilunar Thebesian valve. The great cardiac vein accompanies the anterior interventricular/LAD artery in the anterior interventricular groove, and venae cordis minimae (Thebesian veins) open into all cardiac chambers.

questions.subject: Anatomy
questions.question: In a patient with thrombosis of the coronary sinus, which of the following cardiac veins are least likely to get dilated?
questions.explanation: The anterior cardiac veins are least likely to dilate because they drain directly into the right atrium rather than through the coronary sinus.
questions.structuredExplanationText: The anterior cardiac veins are least likely to dilate because they drain directly into the right atrium rather than through the coronary sinus.

questions.subject: Anatomy
questions.question: Which of these veins does not open into the sinus venarum?
questions.explanation: The small cardiac vein does not open directly into the sinus venarum; it opens into the coronary sinus. The superior vena cava, coronary sinus and inferior vena cava open into the sinus venarum, the smooth posterior part of the right atrium.
questions.structuredExplanationText: The small cardiac vein does not open directly into the sinus venarum; it opens into the coronary sinus. The superior vena cava, coronary sinus and inferior vena cava open into the sinus venarum, the smooth posterior part of the right atrium.

questions.subject: Anatomy
questions.question: Sympathetic innervation of heart is by ______
questions.explanation: Sympathetic innervation of the heart is from T1-T5. Preganglionic sympathetic fibers arise from T1-T5; some synapse in upper thoracic sympathetic ganglia and others in cervical ganglia. Postganglionic fibers from these ganglia form the sympathetic cardiac nerves and innervate the heart.

questions.subject: Anatomy
questions.question: Where is cardiac ganglion situated?
questions.explanation: The cardiac ganglion of Wrisberg is present in the superficial cardiac plexus immediately below and slightly in front of the arch of the aorta, to the right of the ligamentum arteriosum.
questions.structuredExplanationText: The cardiac ganglion of Wrisberg is present in the superficial cardiac plexus immediately below and slightly in front of the arch of the aorta, to the right of the ligamentum arteriosum.
